sections.h2: How would you describe Farmington, Minnesota, to someone selling a home there?
sections.html:
Farmington sits in southern Dakota County on the metro's outer rim, and nearly nine in ten homes are owner-occupied. Mid-2025 Census estimates count 25,425 people, up 7.4 percent from the April 2020 base. Roughly 14.6 square miles of land make up the city, which touches Lakeville on its west side, Empire Township on the east, and Castle Rock and Eureka townships to the south.

Locals split town along County Highway 50. The older downtown lies south of that road, where only a couple of large projects have gone in over two decades. North of it, subdivisions are newer, and a third growth area spreads east into Empire Township. A trail along the Vermillion River ties downtown, uptown and the Empire-side neighborhoods together, a feature worth mentioning in a listing or an offer conversation.

The city got its charter in 1872, making it the second-oldest community in Dakota County after Hastings. A fire on November 22, 1879 destroyed several houses, stores, a hotel and a grain elevator downtown. Growth came late: the 2000 count was 12,365, and by 2010 it had reached 21,086.

sections.h2: What do Farmington's housing numbers say about my sale?
sections.html:
The median owner-occupied home in Farmington is valued at $366,200 in five-year survey data covering 2020 through 2024, and 86.5 percent of housing units are lived in by their owners. A seller here is usually competing with other single-family houses, with few apartments in the mix.

At 27.7 minutes, the average commute is the longest of the four cities in the Census comparison, so many households drive a good distance to their jobs.

Another number worth knowing: 29.1 percent of Farmington residents are under 18, the highest share among the four cities in that comparison, against 24.2 percent in Fridley and 20.8 percent in Inver Grove Heights. Families with children are a large part of the demand, so bedroom count, a fenced yard and nearby schools tend to matter more to buyers here than walkability. Owners without a mortgage report median monthly costs of $781, which is a useful benchmark when a buyer asks what it costs to carry the house.

sections.h2: How do I close out the Farmington city water account when I sell?
sections.html:
Call Farmington Utility Billing at 651-280-6883 before closing to book a final meter reading. The city does not shut water off when someone moves out, so the account keeps running until you close it.

  • Utility bills come quarterly, and the city bills water, sewer, storm water and street lights.
  • Trash and recycling are billed separately by Dick's Sanitation, which handles cancellations at 952-469-2239.
  • Any unpaid final utility bill is certified to the property as a special assessment, so a buyer's title company may hold money back at closing if the account is open.

Landlords selling a rental should know that Farmington keeps rental utility accounts in the owner's name, so the owner has to close the account, not the tenant. A late fee of 10 percent applies to rental accounts that fall behind. Ask Utility Billing for the exact balance on your closing date rather than estimating it from the last bill.

sections.h2: Which schools, roads and employers matter to Farmington buyers?
sections.html:
Farmington Area Public Schools, Independent School District 192, enrolls about 6,900 students. Its attendance area takes in Farmington, eastern Lakeville, and Castle Rock, Empire and Eureka townships. A Lakeville address can therefore sit in a different district, so confirm the district for the exact street before you write a listing.

Main routes are Minnesota Highway 3, Minnesota Highway 50, and Dakota County Roads 31 and 50. A federal air traffic control center for the upper Midwest operates here, and a Kemps packing plant is another long-standing employer. The Dakota County Fairgrounds, about 360 acres with gates on 220th Street and Highway 3, report the highest county fair attendance in the state.

  • Price point: the $366,200 median value compares with $452,500 in neighboring Lakeville.
  • Commute: the 27.7 minute average drive to work is long for the metro.

sections.h2: What are the quickest ways to sell a Farmington house?
sections.html:
Three routes exist: an agent listing, a sale handled on your own, or an as-is purchase by a cash buyer. Each one trades speed against price and effort.

  • Agent listing: strongest when the house shows well and you can ride out inspections and a buyer's loan approval.
  • Do it yourself: skips the commission, though marketing, forms and haggling fall to you.
  • Cash buyer: fits inherited houses, deferred repairs, tenant-occupied rentals and owners behind on payments, since the buyer accepts the house in its present state and the closing date can follow your schedule.

Whatever you choose, Minnesota Statutes 513.55 obliges you to hand the buyer a written disclosure of known material facts before a purchase agreement is signed. Condition questions differ by area: subdivisions north of County Highway 50 are mostly under twenty years old, while downtown houses are older.

sections.h2: What happens at the Dakota County recorder when a Farmington deed is filed?
sections.html:
The county's records office in Hastings handles every Farmington deed. Walk-in filing is by appointment at the Administration Center, and mailed packets go to 1590 Highway 55 in Hastings with a return envelope. Most parcels countywide are abstract property, so your title company will search the record before closing.

Minnesota's deed tax equals the net sale price times 0.0033. At Farmington's $366,200 median, expect about $1,208. A deed also has to carry a well disclosure certificate, or a line stating the seller knows of no wells (Minnesota Statutes 103I.235). Before a deed is accepted, the county auditor looks for delinquent taxes (Minnesota Statutes 272.12). Recording charges are fixed by state law and posted on the county's fee page, so your title company can quote the total.

sections.h2: When are Farmington property taxes due, and who pays at closing?
sections.html:
Dakota County bills in two installments, May 15 and October 15 in 2026, and the autumn one is now behind us. A missed half costs 2 percent on a homestead and 4 percent otherwise, with monthly additions through December (Minnesota Statutes 279.01).

Settlement statements normally split the current year's bill between buyer and seller by closing date. Check the county's parcel search for open balances ahead of listing. The next homestead application deadline is December 31.

If you owe back taxes, the county treasurer can tell you the payoff, and the title company will usually pay it from your proceeds at the closing table. Keep your latest tax statement handy so you can confirm the parcel number and the amounts already paid.

faqs.q: How quickly can I close on a Farmington house?
faqs.a: A cash purchase can close on a date you choose, frequently within a few weeks, since no lender appraisal is involved. Listing with an agent generally runs longer. For either path, book the water meter reading with Farmington Utility Billing in advance.

faqs.q: Are repairs required before I sell in Farmington?
faqs.a: The disclosure statute asks for a written statement of material facts you know before a purchase agreement is signed, and it does not list required repairs. Cash buyers take the house as it stands. Retail buyers often negotiate fixes after an inspection.

faqs.q: What becomes of an unpaid Farmington utility bill after a sale?
faqs.a: It stays attached to the property. The city certifies unpaid water, sewer, storm drainage and street light charges as a special assessment, so buyers' title companies usually want the last bill settled. A final read keeps the number accurate.

faqs.q: Who files the deed for a Farmington sale?
faqs.a: Dakota County's records office in Hastings, normally through your title company. The state sets the fees, the deed tax is 0.0033 of the net price, and the deed needs either a well certificate or a no-wells statement.

faqs.q: Can I sell Farmington rental property while tenants live there?
faqs.a: Yes. Go over the lease terms with the buyer and your title company. Farmington keeps rental utility accounts in the owner's name, so plan to close that account on the sale date.
